# AI-Valid | AI Readiness Audit 🛡️
> A comprehensive guide and technical documentation for the AI-Valid tool.

## Overview
**AI-Valid** is a professional, high-fidelity auditing tool designed to evaluate how "AI-ready" your website or platform is. As the web transitions from human-only consumption to autonomous agent interaction, AI-Valid helps developers and business owners ensure their data is accessible, correctly signaled, and compatible with modern AI standards.

## Key Features
- **Weighted readiness score**: A percentage of the weight actually available, with a letter grade and a per-category breakdown, rather than a raw count of passing checks.
- **Prioritised fixes**: A ranked shortlist of the failures that would move the score most, each with a ready-to-use remediation prompt.
- **Semantic Protocol Discovery**: Automatically scans for `.well-known` manifests including MCP (Model Context Protocol), A2A Agent Cards, API Catalogs (RFC 9727), and AI Plugins.
- **Bot Accessibility Audit**: Validates `robots.txt` and explicit AI directives for `OAI-SearchBot`, `GPTBot`, and others.
- **Content Optimization**: Checks for Content Negotiation (Markdown support), server-side rendering, structured data and legal usage signals via `Content-Signal` headers.
- **MCP server**: The auditor itself is callable as a tool from any MCP client.
- **Actionable Dashboard**: Results are categorized into **Passed**, **Warnings**, & **Not found**, providing a clear implementation roadmap.
- **Deep Linking**: Share audit results easily via persistent URL hashes.

## How the score works
Every check carries a weight reflecting how much it actually matters, from 10 (table
stakes — a site that misses these is invisible or unreadable to agents) down to 1 (niche
protocols that only apply to some sites). The score is the percentage of available weight
earned, so a niche miss barely moves the number while a missing title tag does.

Checks that report a **policy choice** rather than a defect — whether to block AI training,
whether to declare a TDM reservation — are marked `advisory` and excluded from the score
entirely. Deciding to welcome AI training is a legitimate business decision, and the audit
reports it without penalising it in either direction.

A resource that exists but is gated behind authentication earns partial credit rather than
nothing.

## Technology Stack
- **Backend**: Cloudflare Workers (High-performance, global edge deployment).
- **Frontend**: Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), Modern CSS (Glassmorphism), and Semantic HTML5.
- **Deployment**: Wrangler CLI.
- **Performance**: Zero external dependencies on the frontend for lightning-fast loads.

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites
- Node.js
- Wrangler CLI

### Installation
```bash
git clone git@github.com:SecH0us3/ai-valid.git
cd ai-valid/ai-valid
npm install
```

### Local Development
```bash
npx wrangler dev
```

### Deployment
```bash
npx wrangler deploy
```

## API Reference

### `GET /api/audit`
Perform an AI readiness audit on a given origin.

**Query Parameters:**
- `targetUrl` (required): The URL of the website to audit (e.g. `https://example.com`). Only the origin is used.
- `format`: `json` (default) or `md` for a Markdown report. Equivalent to the `Accept` header.
- `bypassCache`: `true` to re-run the audit instead of serving a cached result.

**Content negotiation:** send `Accept: text/markdown` to receive a Markdown report. Responses
carry `Vary: Accept`.

**Responses:**
- `200 OK`: Audit results — see the response shape below.
- `400 Bad Request`: Missing or malformed `targetUrl`, or the origin is unreachable.
- `403 Forbidden`: The target resolves to a private or restricted network address.
- `429 Too Many Requests`: Rate limit exceeded; honour `Retry-After`.
- `500 Internal Server Error`: Server error.

**Response shape:**
- `score`: `{ total, max, grade, earnedPoints, possiblePoints, categories }`. `total` is a
  percentage; `max` is always 100.
- `priorities`: the highest-weight failing checks, most impactful first.
- `bots`, `content`, `protocols`: each with a `results` array. Every check carries `name`,
  `status` (`ok` / `warn` / `err`), `code`, `message`, `weight`, `category`, `prompt` and
  `spec`; advisory checks additionally carry `advisory: true`.

### `POST /mcp`
Model Context Protocol endpoint, JSON-RPC 2.0 over streamable HTTP. Supports `initialize`,
`ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`.

```bash
curl -X POST https://ai-valid.secmy.app/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"audit_website","arguments":{"targetUrl":"https://example.com"}}}'
```

The single tool `audit_website` takes `targetUrl` (required) and `format` (`summary` or
`full`), and returns both a readable summary and `structuredContent` with the score and
priorities. Discovery metadata is at `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm test        # 161 tests
npx wrangler dev
```

## Specifications Audited
AI-Valid audits against several emerging and established standards:
- llms.txt (https://llmstxt.org/)
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
- RFC 9727 (API Catalog) (https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9727)
- Agent Skills (https://agentskills.io/)
